title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching has significantly reduced per-token cost but introduced scenarios where long-running streams or adversarial traffic can starve short latency-sensitive requests. This PR introduces scheduler-level tuning aimed at improving queueing fairness, preventing request starvation, and adding adaptive timeouts for queued requests so we meet p95/p99 latency SLOs without sacrificing throughput.

Summary of changes: consolidated fairness queueing logic into a single scheduler component; added per-priority sub-queues with aging-based promotion; introduced a starvation detector that triggers forced dispatch if a request exceeds a configurable wait threshold; implemented adaptive queue timeouts that scale based on current batch occupancy and recent dispatch latencies; added several new config knobs for operators to tune (see config section); adjusted default values to conservative settings based on canary runs.

Key design notes: - Fairness is implemented with per-priority queues (latency, balanced, throughput) and an aging counter that promotes queued items after X ms of waiting. This prevents low-priority continuous streams from dominating the batch window. - Starvation prevention: a background monitor scans queue wait times and can preempt batch composition to include starved entries at a small throughput cost. The monitor respects per-customer isolation and capacity guards so it cannot violate SLAs for dedicated capacity. - Adaptive timeouts: rather than a fixed queue timeout (previously 50ms), the scheduler computes a target wait budget using a moving average of recent dispatch latencies and current in-flight batch occupancy. This reduced wasted cycles from assembling underpopulated batches while avoiding large latency spikes. - Backwards compat: All knobs are opt-in via the batcher config. The new scheduler can be enabled cluster-wide or per-deployment. Default config mirrors current behavior with small improvements, so rollout is safe for hosted customers.

Benchmarks and results: Canary tests on production-like workloads (mixed short chat, long generation, high-concurrency embedding fanout) show: p50 latency: -1% (small), p95 latency: -12% improvement, p99 latency: -18% improvement for latency-priority requests, overall throughput: +8-14% depending on model and sequence length distribution, CPU/GPU utilization: +3% on average due to slightly denser batching. Bench harness and raw numbers are in benchmarks/continuous-batcher/throughput_latency.md.

Config additions (defaults in parentheses): - scheduler.mode (auto) - scheduler.priority_queues.enabled (true) - scheduler.aging_promotion_ms (150) - scheduler.starvation_threshold_ms (400) - scheduler.adaptive_timeout.enabled (true) - scheduler.adaptive_timeout.alpha (0.2) - scheduler.max_preempt_frequency_per_sec (5)

Testing and rollout plan: Unit and integration tests added. End-to-end canary run against 5% traffic for 48 hours followed by progressive rollout to 50% and then 100% if no regressions. Metrics added to observability for queue_wait_time, promoted_count, starvation_preempt_count, adaptive_timeout_value. Alerts: SLO-regression alert tied to p99 latency and promotion rate anomaly.

Risk and mitigation: Preemption can slightly reduce throughput for tight GPU utilization cases; we default to conservative thresholds and expose knobs. If customers need old behavior, cluster operators can toggle scheduler.mode to legacy.

Notes: This PR focuses on scheduler policy; kernel/execution runtime changes are out of scope but will be coordinated in follow-ups (ENG-1302).

review_comments: Ethan Chen: Can you explain how aging_promotion_ms was chosen? It seems high for low-latency workloads.
Priya Nair: We ran a sweep across five representative traffic shapes; 150ms minimizes p99 regressions while keeping promotion rate low. Benchmarks attached in the canary doc show sensitivity curves.
Lucas Martinez: Starvation detector uses a background scan. Could that become a hot path? Any contention concerns?
Priya Nair: The detector runs at a low frequency (configurable) and uses lock-free snapshots of queue head timestamps; added microbenchmarks show negligible contention under high QPS.
Olivia Park: Request-level isolation note — ensure we don't violate dedicated capacity per-tenant limits during preemption. How is that enforced?
Priya Nair: Preemption honors per-tenant concurrency caps and the capacity guard checks before forcing inclusion; added tests to validate this in integration suite.
Ethan Chen: Please add a short paragraph in docs about rollback steps if we see throughput regressions.
Priya Nair: Added rollback steps and conservative flags in docs/running/continuous-batcher.md.
Ethan Chen: LGTM, happy to approve after CI green and a canary run.
Olivia Park: Approved with no comments.
release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduling: fairness via aging promotion, starvation prevention, and adaptive queue timeouts.
Default settings are conservative; operators can tune scheduler.* knobs in runtime config.
Added observability metrics for queue_wait_time, promoted_count, and starvation_preempt_count.
